pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/history.rs:390 The audit-action guard stops reading each file at its first #[cfg(test)], and because service.rs has that attribute on a struct field at line 175 and engines.rs on a statement at line 474, the live writers owner.decision (service.rs:693) and run.finish (engines.rs:481) are never read, so a new writer placed after those points would ship unclassified with the test green.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/history.rs:390 A raw text split stands in for 'what executes'. Measured by re-running the same logic: 13 of 190 scanned files have a non-module #[cfg(test)] first, and the scan sees 56 action literals where 58 exist. Both hidden actions happen to have rows today, so the result is green by luck.

crates/table-runtime/src/history.rs:391 Only two literal spellings are recognised and any other form (a constant, format!, a variable) is silently not a writer rather than a failure, while the doc comment at line 377-378 claims a new writer file cannot escape the check.

crates/table-runtime/src/history.rs:849 Only written-to-row is asserted; row-to-writer is not. Three rows (money.resent, money.parked, edited.offline) have no literal writer in the tree. They may be kept for older ledgers, but no exclusion entry says so.
crates/table-runtime/src/history.rs:385 The walk asserts its instrument with a file floor, and line 848 adds a floor on actions found, so an empty scan cannot pass.
crates/table-runtime/src/history.rs:380 The guard's verdict is a function of the checked-out tree only, so it has earned the right to block.
crates/table-runtime/src/reached_paypal_tests.rs:533 The agreement between the two copies is mechanised as a test rather than left as a convention.
crates/table-runtime/src/safety.rs:71 The total is taken from the full population before the display cap at line 87, so the cap is not consumed as a data cap.
crates/table-runtime/src/limits.rs:82 Limits that cannot be verified are a hole in the gate's vision and resolve to a distinct Unverified status with money out refused, not to no limits.

pairs.registryProposal: match-the-resolved-artifact could name a further variant: truncating a file at the first occurrence of a test-only marker, on the assumption it opens a trailing test module. In languages where the same attribute also decorates single fields and statements, this silently discards production code, and comment stripping does not catch it.
